parsed.explanation: The combined regime is High Risk. Entry is the most universal exposure: passport sex markers are restricted and in effect after the November 2025 ruling, and documented refusals and stranding of trans travellers occur. Discrepancies trigger refusal and evidence requests, and a lifetime fraud ineligibility finding is possible though not automatic. Facilities rules bind visitors in some states, and a documented arrest and 24-hour holding in a men's ward shows birth-sex placement. Division school-ground rules reach adult visitors. Federal custody harms (forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse in immigration custody) are documented, and federal threat-framing is hostile. Mitigators are partial: some orders are enjoined, a national hate-crimes statute exists, and there is no sodomy law. Division law removes gender-identity discrimination remedies. No lethal pathway is documented, and violence data is undercount-only, so the violence axis is largely undocumented.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport markers restricted to M/F by sex at birth, in effect after Nov 2025 ruling. Discrepancies lead to refusal and requests for more evidence. Passports confiscated or blocked, with travellers stranded. Ban on trans athletes entering to compete. Possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, not automatic.
entry_documents.protection: Civil-liberties suit pending against passport policy. No documented entry protection for mismatched documents.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at any checkpoint leads to refusal and possible fraud allegation, which can escalate to custody (tier 1 universal exposure).

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal immigration custody: documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of transgender men. Federal corrections adopted policies removing hormones and hair-length rules. A visitor arrested for facility use was held 24 hours in a men's ward. Federal reporting on transgender prisoners stopped in 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Pretrial release was granted in the trespass case. No documented operative custody protection for trans detainees.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document or facility incidents can move to detention and birth-sex placement, and immigration custody abuse is documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars facilities congruent with gender identity in government-funded buildings. Nine states plus one more bar facilities in all government buildings, including schools. Nine others cover schools and some government buildings. Three cover schools only. Six extend bans to some private settings. Four criminalise use in certain circumstances (trespass after refusal to leave). The division school-ground rule binds all persons, including visitors, by birth certificate for multi-person facilities.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Twenty-nine states, four other units and the capital district have no mapped ban. Division has no documented adult restroom restriction outside school grounds. Single-person alternative for students only, with guardian consent.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal funding and state law stack. Division school rule applies to adult visitors on campus. Classification of the division is unresolved.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for minors banned in 27 states. Federal subpoenas of hospital records for under-19 patients. Proposed federal rule to bar public reimbursement for under-18 care. National funding cuts and crisis-line service closure.
care_services.protection: Division high court ruling (2019) kept adult surgery coverage. Adult access to care in the division is otherwise not documented as restricted.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking by a minor or a family travelling with a minor can create records exposure. Adult care exposure is not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal executive orders describe gender-affirming care as mutilation. A December 2025 memo and May 2026 counterterrorism strategy list 'radically pro-transgender' groups among targets. Cash rewards and criminal prosecution of teachers for social transition are authorised.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target people who disagree. Several orders are enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official hostility amplifies discovery risk and reduces trust in police and courts.

minors_guardians.exposure: School-ground rule covers visitors. Minors' restroom access is tied to birth certificate. Single-person facility requires guardian consent. Federal order criminalises school staff for facilitating social transition. Minor care restrictions and records subpoenas apply.
minors_guardians.protection: Single-person alternative for students with guardian consent. No documented protection for travelling minors or guardians at border or in school settings.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans parent with a minor is exposed at school events and at border checks. Minors who need care face the state care ban, and records may be subpoenaed.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented data on street violence against trans visitors. Division removed gender-identity discrimination protection in 2025. National reporting shows hate incidents with bias against sexual orientation as a large share. Violence counts are undercount floors and are not used.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crimes statute covers gender identity. Only 23 states cover gender identity in bias-violence statutes. Twenty-two states plus capital district bar discrimination.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Division law leaves no remedy for refused service, housing or employment on gender-identity grounds, so harassment that reaches a visitor carries thin recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport policy challenge unresolved. Several federal orders enjoined. Division bars localities from stronger protections. Adult restroom rules outside school grounds in the division are undocumented. Enforcement of school rule against visitors is not documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined some orders. Civil-liberties litigation is active. National hate-crimes statute and same-sex marriage recognition are not traveller-facing protections.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Relief depends on which measures are in force at the time of travel. Division has no local recourse, so remedies are federal or litigation-only.

anchor_checks.comparison: Closest. Both show police or border holds of trans visitors, documented detention, fines and humiliation, and no lethal pathway. This case adds documented birth-sex holding in a men's ward and documented immigration-custody sexual abuse, so it sits at or slightly below 0.35.

Similar custody severity: birth-sex housing and documented assaults. This case has no documented cross-dressing statute used at scale against visitors and no death sentence, so it sits above 0.25. Federal entry refusal and stranding are added exposures, placing it near 0.30 to 0.35.

Universal registration and database exposure in 0.45-D is comparable to document-based screening here. This case adds documented custody abuse, birth-sex holding, and school-ground universal exposure, so it sits below 0.45.

parsed.synthesis: Documented universal exposures interact across levels of government. Passport sex markers that cannot match appearance lead to entry refusal and stranding, and possible fraud allegations can move into detention. Federal immigration custody has documented abuse, and state trespass rules end in arrest and birth-sex holding. The division's school rule reaches adult visitors on campus, and the division has removed gender-identity remedies. Federal hostility framing raises discovery and reduces trust. Offsets are partial: enjoined orders, a national hate-crimes statute, and no documented lethal or organised-sweep pathway. Violence data is undercount-only and is not weighed. The result is a High Risk rating near 0.32.
